newsitem.title: USA: Japan should avoid raising interest rates now--IMF.
newsitem.headline: Japan should avoid raising interest rates now--IMF.

text.p: Japan should avoid raising interest rates and tightening budget policy for now because it remains unclear whether its economic recovery is strongly under way, a senior IMF official said on Monday.
"We wouldn't at this stage recommend a change in the accomodative monetary policy," the International Monetary Fund official, who declined to be named, told reporters.
"And we wouldn't at this stage recommend to start withdrawing fiscal stimulus," he added.
In a briefing ahead of the IMF/World Bank annual meeting here later this week, the official pronounced the IMF "reasonably satisfied" with Japan's economic performance.

The Japanese economy is recovering at a moderate underlying pace, although the upswing has been "bumpy," he said. It does seem broadly on course for achieving the 3-1/2 percent growth the IMF envisages for this year.
"We are not totally sure that ... the recovery is strongly on its way" he said, adding, "The jury is still out to decide if you need more or less fiscal stimulus."
Starting in 1997, Japan will have to begin thinking about tackling its big budget deficit. "Restrictive fiscal policies will have to be implemented (in the medium term)," he said.
